Lens|Sporting CP: Model and market both see this as close to a coin flip, with Lens a couple of points ahead thanks to playing at home. Both sides are expected to score about 1.5 goals, so a one-goal home win scores best even though 1-1 is the single likeliest score. Confidence is low: any of the three outcomes would be unsurprising.
Sabah|Slavia Praha: Slavia are rated the stronger side by both the model and the bookmakers. Their seven absentees take away about a quarter of their goal production and of their regular defence, which pulls the model back towards Sabah, but Slavia still win in 46% of cases. A narrow away win is the Pick, with 1-1 almost as likely.
Arsenal|Lille: Arsenal are the strongest club in the model's ratings and Lille are expected to score only about 0.6 goals. Both sides miss around a quarter of their goal production (Havertz and Saliba for Arsenal), so the absences roughly cancel out. Model and market agree on a home win at about 75%, the most confident Pick of the Matchday.
Atleti|Man Utd: Model and market agree on Atlético at about 50% at home, with around 1.9 expected goals against 1.3. Neither side has absences that matter. United are good enough to score, which is why 2-1 is preferred to 2-0.
Galatasaray|Barcelona: Barcelona are clear favourites at 67%. Raphinha and de Jong are among absentees worth about a third of Barcelona's goal production, which trims their expected goals by 6%, and the model gives Galatasaray more of a chance at home (24%) than the bookmakers do (12%). Around four goals are expected, so a score with both teams scoring is preferred.
Inter|Club Brugge: Inter are at full strength and expected to score about 2.5 goals at home against under one for Brugge, who miss a regular centre-back. Model (72%) and market (75%) are close on the home win. 2-0 is both the Pick and the likeliest score.
Leipzig|PSV: Goals are expected at both ends: about 2.2 for Leipzig and 1.5 for PSV. PSV miss more than a quarter of both their goal production and their regular defence, more than Leipzig lose, which moves the model to 55% for the home side. The market sits at 54%.
Viking|Bayern München: Bayern are overwhelming favourites at 80%, with more than three expected goals. The model thinks Viking score at home more often than the bookmakers do, which moves the Pick from 0-3 to 1-3. With this many goals expected the exact score is hard to hit, and Confidence in it is the lowest of the Matchday.
Villarreal|Napoli: A balanced match on paper, but Napoli miss about 30% of their goal production and over a quarter of their regular defence. That lifts the model to 48% for Villarreal against 27% for Napoli, a little beyond the market's 45%. A one-goal home win is the Pick.
Feyenoord|Como: Feyenoord miss a quarter of their goal production and a third of their regular defence, the heaviest combined loss of any home side. That moves the model from 40% to 47% for Como, in line with the bookmakers' 50%. A narrow away win is the Pick.
LASK|Liverpool: Liverpool miss more than half of their usual goal production, with Isak, Ekitiké, Szoboszlai and Gakpo all out, the largest loss of the Matchday; the model cuts their expected goals by 15%. They also lost 0-3 at home to Manchester City on Sunday. LASK are weak enough in attack that Liverpool remain 72% favourites, and 0-2 stays the Pick.
Aston Villa|Fenerbahçe: The model is more confident in Villa (68%) than the market (57%). Both sides miss around 30% of their regular defence, which raises the expected goals at both ends without changing the balance. The blend settles at 62% for Villa and a 2-1 home win.
Bodø/Glimt|B. Dortmund: Bodø/Glimt have the largest home-venue boost of all 36 clubs, and Dortmund miss close to a quarter of both their goal production and their regular defence. The model therefore leans to the home side (43% against 35%), while the market gives Dortmund 47%. The blend follows the market to a narrow away win, but this is the Pick where model and bookmakers disagree most on the winner.
Man City|Paris: The model favours City more strongly (53%) than the bookmakers (44%), and the result sits in between at 48%. Neither side has absences that matter. City won 3-0 at Liverpool on Sunday, which is included in the data.
Real Betis|Porto: The lowest-scoring match in the model's view, which makes 1-0 score better than 2-1. Porto miss nearly a quarter of their regular defence, which nudges the model towards Betis (42% against 30%). The market is a little more confident in Betis at 46%.
Roma|Real Madrid: Both defences are badly hit: Madrid miss 44% of their regular defence (Militão, Konaté, Mendy, Asencio) and Roma 36%, mainly goalkeeper Svilar. The model raises the expected goals at both ends and sees an almost even match (37% Roma, 39% Madrid), while the market gives Madrid 51%. The blend picks a Madrid win by 1-2, with goals more likely here than the ratings alone suggest.
S. Bratislava|Stuttgart: Stuttgart are clear favourites at 66%, with over two expected goals. They miss about a fifth of their goal production and a quarter of their regular defence, and the model expects Slovan to score at home more than the market does, hence 1-2 instead of 0-2.
Shakhtar|AEK Athens: The closest match of the Matchday: 39% Shakhtar, 35% AEK, 26% draw. The model leans to Shakhtar and the market slightly to AEK, and neither side's absences change the picture. Few goals are expected, so 1-0 is the Pick, with low Confidence in the outcome.
